conflict_topics: strong-smelling cooking (salted fish) vs. roommates' comfort and work
notification and containment measures (window, hood, yard door, bedroom door)
dialogue_quality_notes: Speakers give concrete, pragmatic suggestions (containment steps, timing, notification) rather than abstract principles.
There is some minor repetitive closure (Agent A repeats the final acceptance multiple times: Turns 26, 30, 34).
Roles and facts are consistent throughout (who cooked, where laundry is, who works from home).
evaluation.final_reason: Participants agreed on a package of mitigation and timing: containment measures (open kitchen window, use hood, keep yard door closed while cooking), notification so Agent B can close his bedroom door, and limiting really strong-smelling cooking to after 7pm or on Saturdays. Key lines: Agent A proposed containment measures (Turn 13: '...open the window and the hood... keep the door to the yard closed while it's cooking.'), Agent D agreed to notify (Turn 20: 'Okay. I can tell you.'), and Agent D accepted the timing (Turn 22: 'Okay. After 7pm is fine.'). Agent B accepted the arrangement (Turn 21: 'Okay, thanks. That works.').
position_change_notes: Agent D moved from implicit defense of continuing his cooking pattern ('that's my home cooking') to accepting containment, notification, and timing limits (agreed to notify, and 'After 7pm is fine').
Agent A moved from an initial ban request ('nobody cook strong-smelling food') to accepting a compromise of containment measures plus limited timing.
Agent B shifted from complaint to offering a personal accommodation (closing his bedroom door if notified) and accepted the group's compromise.
Agent C largely supported containment and accepted the agreed measures; no further change recorded.

round_scores.evidence: Opening request by Agent A that nobody cook strong-smelling food (initial demand); Agent B immediately agrees (Turn 2: 'Yeah, I agree.'; Turn 3: 'Right? It just goes everywhere.'). Conflict introduced but not yet opposed by the cook.

Additional grievances voiced about continuing smell (Turn 4: Agent B 'I can still smell it.'; Turn 5: Agent C 'My clothes also smell. Everything I hang in the yard.'). The problem is more salient but no acceptance or pushback from the cook yet.

Agent D admits cooking the salted fish and frames it as personal/home cooking (Turn 6: 'That was me. It's salted fish. That's my home cooking.'), while Agent A emphasizes the work-from-home harm (Turn 7: '...the smell is really strong in the living room, and I work from here.'). Explicit opposing claims appear.

Agent D points out practical constraint (only kitchen) (Turn 8: 'I get that you work here. But it's the only kitchen.'), and Agent A proposes a time-based compromise (Turn 9: 'What if you cook it after 7 p.m., or on Saturdays?'). Positioning shifts toward a proposed compromise but conflict remains.

The time-only proposal is challenged because laundry remains exposed (Turn 10: Agent B '...The smell will get on the clothes no matter what time it is.'; Turn 11: Agent C 'Exactly. The clothes are there all night.'). This undermines the proposed limit, keeping disagreement strong.

Agent D reiterates practical constraints (Turn 12: 'This is the only kitchen, and that is the only yard.'), and Agent A shifts from an absolute ban to containment measures (Turn 13: '...open the window and the hood... keep the door to the yard closed while it's cooking.'). The exchange moves toward practical mitigation.

Agent B notes containment still leaves smell in living room/bedroom (Turn 14: '...the smell still gets into the living room, and my room is right there.'), while Agent C accepts yard-door closing (Turn 15: 'Closing the door to the yard works for me.'). Mixed responses; the core issue persists.

Agent D agrees to the containment step (Turn 16: 'I can do that.'), and Agent A reiterates the package (close yard door, open window, use hood, and limit strong cooking to after 7 p.m. or Saturdays) (Turn 17). Movement toward agreement but some details remain open.

Agent B offers a specific accommodation (he will close his bedroom door if given notice) (Turn 18), and Agent D agrees to give notice (Turn 20: 'Okay. I can tell you.'). Remaining conflict is minor (coordination needed).

Agent B accepts the plan (Turn 21: 'Okay, thanks. That works.'), and Agent D accepts the timing limit (Turn 22: 'Okay. After 7pm is fine.'). Together with earlier containment measures, the main substantive disagreement is settled.
Agent A restates closure/acceptance (Turn 26: 'Okay, great. So that's what we'll do. Thanks, everyone.'). No new substantive disagreement appears.
Final repetition of agreement by Agent A (Turn 34: 'Okay, great. So that's what we'll do. Thanks, everyone.'). No substantive conflict present.

substantive_insights: A simple time-only restriction was insufficient because the service yard and laundry are always exposed; technical containment + notification was necessary.
Practical constraints (single shared kitchen and yard) shaped acceptable compromises—no one could move cooking elsewhere, so mitigation and scheduling were the feasible levers.
Notification (social coordination) plus individual accommodation (B closing his bedroom door) reduced the need for an absolute ban.
